title: Later Norvo sidemen and the Hollywood recordings
summary: Hank D'Amico, Mucci, Mastren, Jerry Jerome, Lenny Goldstein and others.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: After Slats Long there was Hank D'Amico?
Yes, we got him in Albany. He joined us in Syracuse; he was marvelous. Drank too much, killed him eventually.
Louis Mucci came with us then; then Al Mastren, Carmen's brother, who runs a restaurant in Cohoes now, I think. I have
Bill Miller.
Bill Miller, yes. Who else?
Jerry Jerome was on there for a while; wasn't he?
Yes, he was. I just don't recall the period he was.
There's a recording for September of '37.
Yes, he was.
"Russian Lullaby," "Clap Hands", "Here Comes Charlie."
That's from on the west coast.
In Hollywood; that's right.
Jerry Jerome was there; I'll be darned. Is Lenny Goldstein in that?
Yes, playing alto.
Lenny Goldstein is the father of a famous rock star these days. What does he call himself; Rupert Holmes. Do you know him?
I've heard of him; yes.
Everybody else has, everybody seems to know him so he must be quite famous. Who was the trumpet player in that band?
George Wettling was there for a while.
Yes, that was in New York.
George Berg.
Yes.
He didvery well in the studios.
Jerry Jerome as well. He was a commercial entrepreneur-- commercials entrepreneur.
